subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenClaw stabilize prompt-facing reply delivery and tool presentation across `message_tool_only` turns by moving authority to immutable execution-time policy, or preserve hidden tool schemas and pursue a different cache-stability design?
rationale: The available candidate fix can preserve cache shape, but it intentionally changes the model-visible protected-tool boundary; tests can verify denial but cannot choose the acceptable product and security posture.

options.title: Approve stable presentation after proof
options.body: Adopt session-stable prompt and tool shapes with immutable pre-side-effect denial, contingent on exact-head OpenAI cache proof and explicit acceptance of visible protected schemas.

options.title: Preserve hidden schemas
options.body: Keep unauthorized protected tools absent and require a narrower design that stabilizes delivery instructions without changing the existing inventory boundary.

options.title: Split the work
options.body: Land only a bounded reply-delivery prompt fix if it can preserve current authorization visibility, and track broader tool-catalog stabilization separately.

recommendation.title: Approve stable presentation after proof
recommendation.body: Adopt session-stable prompt and tool shapes with immutable pre-side-effect denial, contingent on exact-head OpenAI cache proof and explicit acceptance of visible protected schemas.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision spans agent runtime, tool policy, and OpenAI Responses behavior covered by recent adjacent merged work.
